thesis: A basic calculator is a tool people trust with money and homework; the interesting part is that it feels like a physical object (weighty keys, a readable display) while never lying about arithmetic.
job: open it, see a zero on the display
type digits and a decimal point, see them appear
pick an operator (+ - × ÷), see which one is pending
type the second number, press equals, read the result
chain operations (2 + 3 × 4 style left-to-right, or equals-less chaining)
repeat equals to repeat the last operation
correct a mistake: backspace, clear entry, all clear
hit an error (divide by zero) and recover
read a long number without it overflowing
glance at the history/expression line to know what was done

principles: state is always visible: pending operator, current entry
big targets, no accidental destructive taps
steps: define each key's effect in each state
tricks: AC becomes C when there is an entry
pressing an operator twice replaces it
backspace only edits the entry being typed
tests: 5 / 0 shows an error, next digit recovers

principles: display is the hero, high contrast, tabular numerals
operator keys distinct from digits, equals the strongest
tests: squint test: display, then equals, then operators

tricks: display value flicks or fades 80 ms on new result
tests: rapid tapping never queues animation lag

principles: one state object, one render function
tricks: round results to 12 significant digits to kill float noise
switch to exponent for very large values

expectations: immediate evaluation chaining left to right

kinds.name: pocket calculator
kinds.what: classic 4x5 key grid, left-to-right immediate execution, single display

kinds.name: tape calculator
kinds.what: adding-machine style with a scrolling tape of past lines

kinds.name: expression calculator
kinds.what: type a full expression and evaluate with precedence

descriptions: display on top spanning full width, keys below in a 4-column grid
zero spans two columns or sits at bottom left
equals at bottom right in accent colour
behaviors: window narrower: calculator keeps max-width 360 to 420 px and centres
display shrinks font when digits exceed about 9

descriptions: Braun-like: off-white body, charcoal digits keys, one orange equals, slim grey function keys
or dark graphite with amber operators
no web fonts: use system stack: ui-rounded, system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, sans-serif; digits in ui-monospace or tabular-nums
behaviors: weight 300 to 500 on display, 500 to 600 on keys

descriptions: short scale-down on active, quick return
state machine: entering first, operator chosen, entering second, result shown
percent: with a pending op a+b% means b% of a; alone it divides by 100
behaviors: digit after result starts new number
operator after result continues with it

3: preventDefault on slash for quick find

behaviors: pressed key visually flashes its on-screen twin

descriptions: error text short, in display, clears on next input

anti_keywords.instead: explicit state machine with a pure compute function
one committed material: Braun-style off-white and orange, or graphite and amber

anti_keywords.not: operator shown only after press with no cue

anti_keywords.instead: friendly Error that recovers on next key

checks: Does 5 / 0 show an error and recover?
Does a long number stay inside the display?
Do keyboard digits, operators, Enter, Backspace and Escape work?
Is every key a labelled button with a focus ring?
Does it fit at 320 px wide?
